absorbed.basis: direct — the current consumer-pull vendoring model ({#mission-control-issue-contract-consumer-sync}) only detects drift when the consumer's own CI runs check_issue_contract_parity.py; nothing on the producer side pushes a refresh toward registered consumers, which is exactly how the #222 stale-mirror incident (343 clean cards) went unnoticed.

direct — same #222 stale-mirror incident; the existing byte-parity check cannot express which specific fields a consumer actually depends on, so a provider rename of an unrelated field is indistinguishable from one that breaks a real dependency.

external — aviation NOTAM broadcast pattern (moonshot-tier idea); not every registered consumer needs a code-bearing refresh PR, some only need notification that a named contract changed, which is a lighter delivery mode on the same registry.

executor_profile.justification: Matches the issue-map's own executor recommendation. Two coordinated CLI scripts (a registry-driven dispatcher with two delivery modes, and a field-level manifest guard) plus a real conversion of an existing production consumer (mission-control's issue-contract vendoring) without breaking its existing byte-parity gate -- higher-context mechanical-plus-integration work than a single-script build, warranting high effort over medium, but a well-understood existing-gate extension rather than open-ended architectural judgment, so sonnet/inline is sufficient without cross-subsystem reviewer consensus.

source_artifact.content_excerpt: Inverts the propagation burden the consumer-graph issue only maps: producer dispatches refresh PRs on contract change, consumers publish Pact-style expectations the provider CI honors; NOTAM broadcast is the same push model at moonshot scale.
source_artifact.title: Producer-push contract propagation: source repo opens refresh PRs; consumer-driven contract tests
